boundary.description: The api service running in the compose stack, driven over HTTP, with a real Postgres.
boundary.rationale: Compose declares both services and the api is externally reachable; Stripe is the only dependency that cannot be run locally.

scenarios.title: Cancelling a placed order marks it cancelled and refunds nothing else
scenarios.boundary: HTTP against the api service with a real Postgres; Stripe stubbed

preconditions.state: an order exists for the acting customer
preconditions.via: POST /orders, capturing the returned order id
preconditions.assert_established: response is 201 and the body contains a non-empty id
preconditions.rationale: Order creation is journey J1, already under test, and ids are server-generated so they cannot be chosen.

preconditions.state: the order is older than the 24-hour free-cancellation window
preconditions.via: UPDATE orders SET created_at = now() - interval '48 hours' WHERE id = $1
preconditions.rationale: The state is produced only by the passage of time and is unreachable through the public interface.

assertions: the stubbed Stripe client received exactly one refund call for the order total
negative_assertions: no other order belonging to the customer changed status

cleanup: truncate orders, order_items, customers after the test

determinism_controls: inject the age rather than sleeping
poll GET /orders/{id} until status settles, with a bounded timeout; never sleep a fixed duration
new_helpers_needed: a stub Stripe client recording refund calls
open_assumptions: the compose stack starts cleanly on a developer machine
the migrations directory is the complete schema

scenarios.title: Every response carries a non-empty X-Request-Id header
scenarios.boundary: HTTP against the api service with a real Postgres; Stripe stubbed

preconditions.state: an order exists so a 200 and a 404 can both be exercised
preconditions.via: POST /orders, capturing the returned order id
preconditions.assert_established: response is 201 and the body contains a non-empty id
preconditions.rationale: The requirement is about every response, so the check needs both a hit and a miss.

steps: GET /orders/{id} for an id that does not exist
assertions: the 200 response carries a non-empty X-Request-Id header
the 404 response carries a non-empty X-Request-Id header
negative_assertions: the two responses do not carry the same X-Request-Id

cleanup: truncate orders, order_items, customers after the test

determinism_controls: assert the header is non-empty rather than asserting a specific value
open_assumptions: the compose stack starts cleanly on a developer machine
